items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: And from Lucky Millinder, this is when I left Lucky Millinder and went with Lionel Hampton, see? And I played with Lionel Hampton five years

ctx.x: And then, tell us how you got to work with Basie.

Oh, to get to work with Basie was much longer after that. From Jimmie Lunceford, I went with Lucky Millinder’s orchestra, who had Lil Green and many — Bull Moose Jackson and all of these great artists. And from Lucky Millinder, this is when I left Lucky Millinder and went with Lionel Hampton, see? And I played with Lionel Hampton five years, which again was breaking ground into becoming a name out there, but then after leaving Lionel Hampton, in which Lionel Hampton was a band that you played over time a very,…

Share with us just a moment, what it was like traveling from city to city at that time. Give us a year, some of the years of your travel, like let’s say ‘47 or ‘55 or whatever, and tell us what it was like for traveling musicians at that time.

items.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: we’ve got Al Grey playing trombone

ctx.x: Buddy Tate is not playing. But maybe it will come to me after. We’ve got Sweets Edison playing one trumpet, and we’ve got Al Grey playing trombone and oh, this is all changed up.
Yeah. You’ve got Junior Mance on piano?
